full_judgment: 4. The defendants contested the suit by fling written statement contending, inter-alia, that the bainapatra is not correct. In fact the suit land has been mortgaged and the said document executed for mortgage by receiving Taka, 2,500/- the plaintiff. The suit land was khas land of the Government and the defendant did not get settlement of the said land at the time of execution of the bainapatra, so the question of sale did not arise at all. Later on 9.4.1968 the defendants got settlement. The loan amount was to be refunded with 10% interest. The plaintiff of back Taka 2,900 on 15.2.1968. Later on the defendant was asked to depose falsely in a case and when he refused enmity developed between the plaintiff and the defendant and the instant suit was filed. It is asserted by the defendant that there was no agreement for sale with the plaintiff. The plaintiffs suit wag false and vexatious.
